Index Correlation Matrix

Percentile Ranks (All-Time, 10Y, 5Y): The current index value is ranked against all historical daily values within the respective lookback window. A percentile of 80 means the index is at or above 80% of all daily readings in that period (readings ≤ current ÷ total, current point included).

Z-Score: Computed as (current value - mean of same calendar trading day across all years) / standard deviation. Values above +2 or below -2 indicate statistically unusual levels relative to seasonal norms.

Rate of Change (ROC): The percentage change in the index over a rolling 20-trading-day window, indicating short-term momentum.

Max Drawdown: The maximum percentage decline from any peak to subsequent trough within the selected lookback window.

Algorithmic Signal: The signal badge is derived from a combination of 5Y percentile rank, 252-day Z-score, and all-time rank. Backtested on BDI since 1991 (n=8,930): SELL (>80th pct) preceded −1.1% avg fwd 3M vs +7.5% unconditional; GOLDEN DIP +21.4%, VALUE TRAP +23.9% (69% win), and CATCHING KNIFE +32.6% (75% win) — deep-distress labels flag volatility risk, but historically marked the strongest forward-return zones in this strongly mean-reverting index.

Guinea Bauxite Flow (11,200 nm): 14.0 Mt/mo (+22%)
Brazil Iron Ore Flow (11,000 nm): 38.0 Mt/mo (+10%)
Global Port Congestion Factor: 4.5% Fleet Anchored
Mechanism: Guinean Bauxite transits ~11,200 nautical miles to China, consuming 3.11x more Capesize DWT-days per metric tonne than Western Australian iron ore (3,600 nm). When active fleet utilization breaches 88%–90%, spot rate price elasticity accelerates exponentially.
Feasibility note: gray/infeasible zones — Guinea >16 Mt/mo and Brazil >40 Mt/mo exceed observed/model range; slider extremes are diagnostic stress-tests only (sliders retained).
Data provenance (diagnostic): Brazil live (ComexStat), Guinea live (UN Comtrade), WAus fixed 48 Mt/mo assumption, fleet 815 Bn Ton-NM calibrated — see scripts/scrapers/generate_ton_mile_matrix.py.
